chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was traveling, and there was an old man who said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who catches the Imam at Jam' (the gathering place before Arafat)?' He said to him: 'If he thinks that he will go to Arafat and stand there for a little while, then catch Jam' before the sunrise, let him go to it. And if he thinks that he will not reach it until the people depart from Jam', then let him not go to it, for his Hajj is complete.'

key_terms.جَمْع: Jam', the gathering place near Mecca where pilgrims gather before proceeding to Arafat
key_terms.حَجُّهُ: His Hajj, referring to the ritual pilgrimage
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْس: Sunrise, the time marker for the validity of the standing at Arafat
key_terms.عَرَفَات: Arafat, the plain where the essential standing (wuquf) of Hajj takes place
key_terms.يُفِيضَ النَّاس: The people depart, referring to the departure of the crowd from Jam'

ai.seo_question: What should a latecomer do if he catches the Imam at Jam' during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of the 'standing at Arafat' (Wuquf) as the essential pillar of Hajj, distinguishing between the ritual gathering at Jam' and the actual spiritual presence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that if a latecomer can still witness the Imam's brief stand before sunrise, he must join to complete the pillar; otherwise, his Hajj is deemed valid without it, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Imam's presence as a condition for the validity of the ritual in many juristic views. This ruling underscores the flexibility within the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools' broader consensus while highlighting the specific Shia jurisprudential nuance regarding the necessity of the Imam's Wuquf.
